states.name: Pescara

states.name: Chieti
timeline: The Frentani of the Adriatic coast, allies of Rome

states.name: Campobasso

states.name: Foggia
timeline: The Latin colony of Luceria and the Daunian towns of northern Apulia

states.name: Barletta-Andria-Trani
timeline: Canusium and the Apulian towns, allies of Rome

states.name: Bari
timeline: Peucetian towns of central Apulia, allies of Rome

states.name: Brindisi
timeline: Brundisium and the Messapians, conquered in 267–266 BC

states.name: Lecce
timeline: The Sallentini of the heel of Italy, conquered in 267–266 BC

states.name: Taranto

states.name: Matera

states.name: Vibo Valentia
timeline: Hipponium and the Bruttian towns of the Tyrrhenian coast

states.name: Potenza
timeline: Lucanian hill country and the Latin colony of Venusia

states.name: Salerno
timeline: Paestum, a Latin colony since 273 BC, and Greek Velia, a naval ally

states.name: Naples
timeline: Greek Neapolis, which lends Rome ships and crews

states.name: Caserta
timeline: Capua and the Campanian plain, with partial Roman citizenship

states.name: Latina
timeline: Latin and Volscian towns, long tied to Rome; Antium, a Roman colony on the coast

states.name: Rome
timeline: Rome, head of a confederacy of Italian cities and peoples

states.name: Viterbo
timeline: Southern Etruria; Rome destroys rebellious Volsinii in 264 BC

states.name: Grosseto
timeline: Etruscan Vulci and Rusellae, allies of Rome by treaty

states.name: Livorno
timeline: Etruscan Populonia, an iron-working port allied to Rome

states.name: Pisa
timeline: Pisae, an Etruscan and Ligurian port on Rome's northern frontier

states.name: Trapani
timeline: Lilybaeum, Drepana and Eryx, the heart of Punic Sicily
Segesta kills its Punic garrison and goes over to Rome
Duilius relieves Segesta, besieged by the Carthaginians
Hamilcar razes Eryx and moves its people to Drepana

states.name: Messina
timeline: The Mamertines, Campanian mercenaries, hold Messana and call on Rome for help
Allied to Rome since 264 BC, Messana is the Roman bridgehead into Sicily
Duilius wins the battle of Mylae off this coast

states.name: Palermo
timeline: Panormus, Carthage's great harbour on the north coast

Roman consuls march on Panormus and storm Hippana

states.name: Agrigento
timeline: Agrigentum, allied to Carthage, is where the Punic army musters
Two consular armies besiege Agrigentum; Hannibal Gisco holds the city
Agrigentum falls; twenty-five thousand of its people are sold as slaves

states.name: Caltanissetta
timeline: Sicel and Greek hill towns of the interior

Mytistratum falls after a long Roman siege

states.name: Ragusa
timeline: Camarina, an independent Greek city on the south coast

The Romans breach Camarina's walls with Hiero's siege engines

states.name: Syracuse
timeline: Hiero II rules Syracuse and besieges Messana with Carthage
Hiero makes peace with Rome and becomes its ally for fifteen years

states.name: Catania
timeline: Catana and the plain below Etna lie in Syracuse's sphere
Catana surrenders to the consul Valerius

states.name: Carbonia-Iglesias
timeline: Sulci, an old Phoenician port, and the silver-lead hills of Iglesias
Hannibal's fleet is destroyed at Sulci; his own men crucify him

states.name: Sassari
timeline: Nuragic communities of the north-west, beyond firm Punic control

states.name: Nuoro
timeline: Mountain country of independent Sardinian peoples

states.name: Olbia-Tempio

states.name: Oristano

states.name: Medio Campidano
timeline: The grain plains of the Campidano, farmed for Carthage

states.name: Cagliari
timeline: Karalis, Carthage's chief city in Sardinia

states.name: Ogliastra
timeline: Independent Sardinian peoples of the eastern mountains

states.name: Enna
timeline: Enna and Centuripa, Sicel hill towns between the powers
Centuripa and the inland towns go over to Rome
Hamilcar takes Enna by betrayal
The consul Atilius retakes Enna

states.name: Benevento
timeline: Beneventum, a Latin colony since 268 BC

states.name: Siena
timeline: Etruscan Clusium and Volaterrae, allies of Rome

states.name: Arezzo
timeline: Etruscan Arretium, an ally of Rome

states.name: Florence
timeline: Etruscan Faesulae, on the edge of Rome's alliance

states.name: Rieti
timeline: The Sabines, made full Roman citizens in 268 BC

states.name: Terni
timeline: Umbrian country guarded by the Latin colony of Narnia

states.name: Perugia
timeline: Etruscan Perusia and Umbrian towns, allies of Rome

states.name: Frosinone
timeline: The Hernici and Volsci of the Liris valley, Roman citizens or allies

states.name: Avellino
timeline: The Hirpini Samnites, allies of Rome

states.name: L'Aquila
timeline: The Marsi, Paeligni and Aequi of the Apennines, allies of Rome

states.name: Isernia
timeline: The Pentri Samnites, bound to Rome by treaty

events.title: Messana calls Rome
events.text: Besieged by Hiero, the Mamertines of Messana ask Rome for help, and the Roman assembly votes to send an army.

events.title: Claudius crosses
events.text: The consul Appius Claudius Caudex ferries his legions over the Strait of Messina; the Punic garrison withdraws.

events.title: Hanno crucified
events.text: Carthage crucifies Hanno, the officer who gave up Messana without a fight.

events.title: Siege of Messana broken
events.text: Claudius drives off Hiero's army, then the Carthaginians camped outside Messana.

events.title: Volsinii destroyed
events.text: In Italy, Rome sacks the Etruscan city of Volsinii and moves its people.

events.title: Valerius in Sicily
events.text: Both consuls cross with four legions; dozens of Sicilian towns go over to Rome.

events.title: Hiero changes sides
events.text: Hiero II makes peace with Rome, pays a hundred talents and becomes its ally.

events.title: Catana's sundial
events.text: Valerius takes Catana and carries its sundial to Rome as a trophy.

events.title: Segesta defects
events.text: Segesta kills its Carthaginian garrison and joins Rome.

events.title: Aesernia founded
events.text: Rome plants a Latin colony at Aesernia in Samnium.

events.title: Carthage musters
events.text: Carthage hires Ligurian, Celtic and Iberian mercenaries and makes Agrigentum its base.

events.title: Siege of Agrigentum
events.text: The consuls Postumius and Mamilius ring the city with two lines of ditches; some fifty thousand people are inside.

events.title: Hanno lands
events.text: A relief army under Hanno marches from Lilybaeum to Heraclea Minoa with some fifty elephants.

events.title: Romans go hungry
events.text: Hanno takes the Roman depot at Herbessus; only Hiero's supplies keep the besiegers fed.

events.title: Battle of Agrigentum
events.text: After two months facing each other, the Romans rout Hanno's army and its elephants.

events.title: The night breakout
events.text: Hannibal Gisco fills the Roman ditches with straw-packed baskets and escapes with his mercenaries.

events.title: City enslaved
events.text: The Romans sack Agrigentum and sell twenty-five thousand of its people into slavery.

events.title: Inland towns waver
events.text: Inland towns turn to Rome, but Carthage's fleet still holds the coast.

events.title: Italy raided
events.text: Carthaginian ships raid the coasts of Italy while Rome has no fleet.

events.title: Rome builds a fleet
events.text: Rome builds a hundred quinqueremes and twenty triremes, copying a captured Carthaginian ship.

events.title: Trap at Lipara
events.text: The consul Scipio and seventeen ships are trapped in Lipara harbour and captured.

events.title: Hannibal's blunder
events.text: Scouting with fifty ships, Hannibal runs into the Roman fleet and loses most of them.

events.title: The raven
events.text: The Romans fit their ships with the corvus, a spiked boarding bridge.

events.title: Battle of Mylae
events.text: Duilius's boarding bridges win Rome's first sea battle; Carthage loses about fifty ships.

events.title: Hannibal escapes
events.text: Hannibal abandons his seven-banked flagship and gets away in a small boat.

events.title: Duilius's column
events.text: Rome honours Duilius with a naval triumph and a column decorated with ships' rams.

events.title: Thermae ambush
events.text: Hamilcar falls on Rome's allies camped near Thermae and kills some four thousand.

events.title: Segesta relieved
events.text: Duilius lifts the siege of Segesta and storms Macella.

events.title: Hannibal survives
events.text: Carthage removes Hannibal from command but spares his life.

events.title: Aleria taken
events.text: The consul Lucius Scipio captures Aleria on Corsica.

events.title: Attack on Olbia
events.text: Scipio raids Sardinia but cannot take Olbia.

events.title: Eryx emptied
events.text: Hamilcar razes Eryx and moves its people to the fortress port of Drepana.

events.title: Enna betrayed
events.text: Hamilcar takes Enna, high in the hills, by betrayal.

events.title: Hannibal in Sardinia
events.text: Hannibal takes a new fleet to defend Sardinia.

events.title: Panormus defied
events.text: The consuls offer battle outside Panormus; the Carthaginians stay behind their walls.

events.title: Hippana stormed
events.text: The Romans storm Hippana and, after a long siege, take Mytistratum.

events.title: Calpurnius's stand
events.text: Near Camarina, the tribune Calpurnius and a few hundred men hold a hill while the trapped army escapes.

events.title: Camarina retaken
events.text: Hiero's siege engines breach Camarina's walls; most of its people are sold.

events.title: Enna retaken
events.text: The consul Atilius recaptures Enna and nearby hill towns.

events.title: Feint toward Africa
events.text: The consul Sulpicius pretends to sail for Africa and draws Hannibal's fleet out.

events.title: Battle of Sulci
events.text: Caught off Sulci, Hannibal's fleet is destroyed or abandoned on the shore.

events.title: Hannibal crucified
events.text: The surviving Carthaginians seize Hannibal and crucify him.

chartNote: Share of the area of today's provinces of Sicily, Sardinia and central and southern Italy, by the power that held most of each province. Loyalties went city by city and towns changed sides, so this is a simplification; regions are today's boundaries. Mainland Italy, Rome's from the start, weighs heavily; the change is in Sicily and Sardinia. Carthage itself, Malta and Corsica are drawn as neighbours.
